name: Hiroshi Ishii
institution: Massachusetts Institute of Technology Media Lab
description: Hiroshi Ishii founded MIT Media Lab's Tangible Media Group and invented the Tangible Bits paradigm — the principle that physical objects should embody digital information and computational control, turning everyday surfaces and objects into interactive interfaces. His group's inForm shapeshifting display table, programmable matter explorations, and radical atoms concept envision a future where material itself becomes dynamic digital media, influencing interaction design research globally. Ishii's work introduced the concept of the 'seamful design' of physical-digital seams and his mediaBlocks system for tangible video manipulation was one of the first deployments of tangible computing in professional media production. He received the ACM SIGCHI Social Impact Award and the Design Award from the Cooper Hewitt Smithsonian National Design Museum. His collaborations with Steelcase produced Roam, a mobile whiteboard system that integrates physical boards with Microsoft Surface Hub digital workspaces.
